passages.note: Bill overview page shows she prime-sponsored HB2756, whose subject is "utilities; high load factor customers", not data centers.
House Final Reading vote page records her Aye and the 39-16 tally, but prints no provision.

passages.provision_quote: An electric public service corporation operating in this state shall file with the corporation commission semiannual reports regarding new extra high load factor customers
passages.note: The enacted text regulates "extra high load factor customers" and never names data centers.

rows.reasoning: The only record on file, HB2756 (2026), which Griffin prime-sponsored and voted for, regulates "new extra high load factor customers" and nowhere names data centers, so under the annex it is not evidence on this ladder. Even read on its content it would not match a rung: the semiannual interconnection reports are not "transparency about projected energy demand and rate impacts", and letting the commission set minimum billing, contract length and customer payments for infrastructure is a cost-sharing arrangement rather than "barring utilities from passing any data center energy infrastructure costs to residential customers".
